name: BSD

phase_0.boundary_condition: The global field of rational numbers and its algebraic closure

VINIT.justification: The state before the definition of the cubic equation coefficients a and b

TANCH.justification: The overarching statement that binds the analytic and algebraic properties into a single identity

AFWD.justification: The process of extending the L-function from the region of convergence to the entire complex plane

AREV.justification: The reduction of the group of rational points to determine the rank via height functions and p-adic methods

CLINK.justification: The mapping from a modular curve to the elliptic curve that links arithmetic and analysis

IMSCRIB.justification: The intrinsic arithmetic invariant that identifies the curve within the modular hierarchy

FSPLIT.justification: The separation of the curve's data into local Euler factors and global analytic behavior

FFUSE.justification: The recombination of local data to produce the leading coefficient and the order of vanishing

EVALT.justification: The condition where the analytic rank matches the algebraic rank

EVALF.justification: The condition where the analytic rank and algebraic rank do not match

ENGAGR.justification: The collection of elements that are locally trivial but globally non-trivial, representing a state of simultaneous existence and obstruction

IFIX.justification: The permanent numerical record of the curve's infinite order points

phase_2.split_input: The elliptic curve E over Q
phase_2.fuse_result: The elliptic curve E over Q

phase_3.void_description: The pre-arithmetic state where no curve or field is defined
phase_3.true_description: The analytic rank equals the algebraic rank
phase_3.false_description: The analytic rank does not equal the algebraic rank
phase_3.both_description: The presence of non-trivial elements in the Tate-Shafarevich group creating a local-global obstruction

steps.domain_action: Define the rational field Q as the base of operations
Specify the coefficients a and b for the elliptic curve equation
Record the discriminant to ensure the curve is non-singular
Branch the curve data into analytic and algebraic paths
Construct the L-function through the product of local Euler factors
Apply the modularity theorem to ensure analytic continuation
Determine the order of vanishing r at the central point s=1
Perform a p-descent to bound the size of the Selmer group
Account for the Tate-Shafarevich group elements that resist direct computation
Identify potential obstructions to the Hasse principle
Recombine the analytic order and algebraic rank into the BSD formula
Commit the final rank and regulator values to the arithmetic record
Close the system under the unified conjecture

phase_5.compiler_frontend: The modularity theorem providing the bridge between forms and curves
phase_5.ipc_mechanism: The Selmer group acting as the interface between local and global data
phase_5.memory_mechanism: The database of elliptic curve isogeny classes and their invariants
phase_5.scheduler_mechanism: The sequence of p-adic valuations and limit processes
phase_5.alfs_store: The Cremona database of elliptic curves

phase_6.cycle_cost: Computational cycles required for point searching and L-series evaluation
phase_6.pre_cycle_state: An unverified relationship between the L-function and the group of points
phase_6.post_cycle_state: A rigid numerical identity between analytic and algebraic invariants
phase_6.delta_s_verdict: ΔS ≈ 0 — The information content of the curve is conserved through the analytic-algebraic transformation
